plan: Trim QQQI to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the single-name mandate.
Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, METU, MUU, MSFU, PLTU, SPAL) to zero for capital preservation.
This strategy prioritizes stability and reduces overall portfolio risk.
Maintain a significant cash buffer for future opportunities.
conservative.read: This conservative plan targets around 1.5% per month, focusing on capital preservation. It significantly reduces risk by eliminating leveraged ETFs and lowering concentration. Expect lower drawdowns but also more modest returns.

plan: Trim QQQI to 25% to meet the single-name mandate.
Reduce exposure to all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, METU, MUU, MSFU, PLTU, SPAL) to small positions.
Buy RTX at 4% as a new quality long setup from the scanner.
This plan balances growth with risk management, maintaining a moderate cash buffer.
balanced.read: This balanced plan aims for approximately 2.5% per month, prioritizing risk-first growth. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while adding a high-quality long setup. Expect moderate volatility and growth potential.

plan: Trim QQQI to 25% to meet the single-name mandate.
Add to all existing leveraged ETFs (SOXL, METU, MUU, MSFU, PLTU, SPAL) to increase exposure.
Buy RTX at 6% as a new quality long setup from the scanner.
This plan aggressively leans into leverage and concentration for higher growth potential.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets around 4% per month, aiming for stretched growth. It significantly increases exposure to leveraged ETFs and concentrates in high-scoring setups. Be aware of substantially higher drawdown risk and the daily decay/rebalancing of leveraged ETFs. Strict stop discipline is critical.

income.read: This income plan targets around 1% per month, focusing on parking cash for yield. It maximizes exposure to income-generating ETFs and eliminates high-beta, leveraged positions. While aiming for steady distributions, NAV can still fall in market downturns, and distributions are not guaranteed.
